sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Customs Clearance Brokerage and Bonded Transit Management

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European codified private law, modified by Luxembourg statutes, EU direct-effect regulations, and settled Luxembourg case law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU Treaty framework (TFEU Articles 49, 54, 63 on freedom of establishment and free movement of capital)
Benelux Union Treaty of 17 June 2008 (in force 2012) and Benelux economic integration instruments
BLEU bilateral investment treaties in force (approx. 80 treaties, including BLEU–Hong Kong SAR 2005, BLEU–Moldova 2000, BLEU–Ethiopia 2006)
Luxembourg double taxation agreements (approx. 84 in force, including LU–US 1996 as amended by the 2009 Protocol, LU–Germany 2012, LU–France, LU–China 1994 as amended by the 2015 Protocol)
EU–Canada CETA (provisional application since 21 September 2017) and EU–Japan EPA (in force 1 February 2019) investment protection chapters

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (SARL regime, Articles 180 et seq.); Law of 12 November 2004 against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing AMLD4/AMLD5; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 31 May 1999 on commercial domiciliation; Union Customs Code Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, Articles 18 and 39 governing customs representation, good repute, and establishment.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted public access; following CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022, the Luxembourg RBE grants access to the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), CSSF, judicial authorities, notaries, lawyers, auditors, and regulated financial institutions performing customer due diligence; public access is limited to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest on a case-by-case basis)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each shareholder and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or competent identity authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Convention of 5 October 1961, in force for Luxembourg since 1979) for non-EU contracting states; Consular Legalization for states not party to the Convention; notarized certified copy acceptable for EU/EEA documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official corporate registry extract for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille with sworn French or German translation; Consular Legalization only where apostille is unavailable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of blocked share capital account or sworn statement of capital subscription (minimum EUR 12,000 for SARL)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution or EEA credit institution with a Luxembourg branch
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original signed bank confirmation; apostille not required for authenticated bank correspondence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract or police clearance certificate for each manager and designated customs representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn French or German translation; subject to UCC Article 39 good-repute and professional-competence assessment by Administration des douanes et accises

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and business address for identity verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, municipal registration office, or bank statement issuer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified/notarized copy; apostille required for documents originating from non-contracting states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory, recurring (event-driven plus at least annual) screening of all UBOs, managers, and customs representatives against: (1) UN Security Council Consolidated Lists; (2) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Lists under Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001 and asset-freeze regimes including Russia and Belarus packages (Regulations (EU) No 269/2014, No 833/2014, No 765/2006); (3) Luxembourg national asset-freeze decisions of the Minister of Finance coordinated by the CRF; (4) OFAC SDN List as a risk-based overlay whenever USD clearing or United States nexus exists. Enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons per the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; written risk assessment, CDD file, and screening results to be retained for 5 years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – www.lbr.lu – electronic RCS filing module (dépôt électronique) and online name reservation service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be composed of Latin-alphabet letters including accented characters; Luxembourgish, French, German, and phonetically transliterated names are permissible. Names originating from non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Hebrew) require a mandatory Latin-character transliteration appearing in the RCS excerpt and all customs and ACH documentation. Official statutory filings are accepted in French and German; LBR business entity data may include English descriptors, but the registered name itself must be in Latin script and must not be misleading as to the company's legal form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Crédit, Caisse d'Épargne, Paiement (CSSF authorization required)
Assurance, Réassurance, Assurance-Vie (Commissariat aux Assurances authorization required)
SICAV, SICAF, FCP, Fonds Commun de Placement, Investment Fund (CSSF authorization required)
Luxembourg, Grand-Duché, État, Commune, Royal, Gouvernement (official-liability implication; prior ministerial consent required)
Chambre de Commerce, Chambre des Métiers, Bourse, Université du Luxembourg

Douane, Douanes et Accises, Customs Authority, Customs Brokers of Luxembourg (official administration misrepresentation risk; prior written authorization from Administration des douanes et accises required)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is effective for 90 days from the online LBR reservation and may be extended once for an additional 90 days at the same administrative fee through the LBR e-Desk prior to expiry. Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant or the notary may: (1) file an informal reconsideration submission with the RCS service within 15 days of the refusal notice; (2) if the refusal is maintained, lodge a formal appeal to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement, commercial chamber) within 30 days of notification, using summary proceedings before a single commercial judge; (3) alternatively, file a fresh name application featuring a distinguishing element (e.g., activity descriptor, corporate or personal surname, geographical suffix) while the court appeal remains pending. Legal basis: Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and on the accounting and annual accounts of undertakings, as amended, and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 on RCS procedures.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for the registered corporate seat only under the Law of 31 May 1999 on commercial domiciliation, provided the domiciliation agent is authorized by the Ministry of Economy. For an ISIC 5229 licensed customs brokerage house, virtual-only substance is insufficient and will be rejected at licensing stage: UCC Article 39 requires a genuine establishment in the customs territory of the Union, operational management, premises, and customs record-keeping infrastructure. A physical Luxembourg office must be maintained for personnel, bonded-transit records, and customs inspection access.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – quantified at 60–75% probability of an unannounced on-site customs or AML inspection within the first 24 months of operations, given the licensed customs-brokerage profile, UCC Article 47 verification powers of the Administration des douanes et accises, and the enhanced Medium-Risk AML tier.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory name availability search and 90-day name reservation via LBR e-Desk
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory flat tariff of EUR 30 plus nominal administrative uplift; market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of SARL articles of association (statuts), shareholders' agreement, and AML/UBO due-diligence file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Luxembourg law firm (avocat à la Cour)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 3,000–EUR 5,000 for standard SARL incorporation with custom provisions; fixed-quoted fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) with statutory capital verification and notary AML/CDD checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff-based fee scale of approximately EUR 1,800–EUR 2,600 for capital at or below EUR 100,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR electronic registration and RCS matricule filing fee (dépôt au registre de commerce et des sociétés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed administrative fee of EUR 75–EUR 130 per Grand-Ducal regulation on RCS filing tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation deed in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / LBR publication service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication price of approximately EUR 120–EUR 150 per filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) first filing identifying the SARL UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory filing price of EUR 75–EUR 85 as published by LBR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization costs for foreign corporate documents (certificate of good standing, passports, criminal records, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign ministries of foreign affairs, Luxembourg consulates, or Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document flat consular fee of EUR 30–EUR 60 applied to 2–4 foreign-origin documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (French or German) of foreign-language incorporation and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Page-based benchmark of EUR 12–EUR 18 per page; typical 20–25 page translation dossier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening and blocked-capital account confirmation for SARL minimum share capital of EUR 12,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg or EEA credit institution with Luxembourg branch
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank administrative and customer-due-diligence fee; recurring account maintenance fees excluded

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Customs representative authorization and UCC indirect-representation registration coordination (dossier preparation, financial guarantee arrangements, AEO readiness assessment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration des douanes et accises and coordinating Luxembourg law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 1,500–EUR 2,500 for UCC Article 39 authorization dossier preparation; no statutory customs filing fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 180-190 and associated transitional provisions governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Grand-Ducal Regulations implementing the RCS electronic filing system.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated under the Ministry of Justice via the eJustice portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif) containing the articles of association (Statuts), filed electronically with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital for a Luxembourg SARL is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation. Cash capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account in the company’s name at a Luxembourg credit institution, and a bank release certificate must be produced to the notary. In-kind contributions require an independent auditor’s valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company accepts the subscriptions to its share capital as recorded in the notarial deed, and the authorized share capital is adopted in accordance with the articles of association. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the articles and the manager(s) named therein are duly confirmed in office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the manager(s) are authorized to open bank accounts, sign agreements, make filings with the RCS, the VAT authority, the customs administration, and social security bodies, and to take all measures necessary for the commencement of business. This resolution takes immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) holding the subscriber’s capital account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary or escrow bank account in the name of the future SARL. Wire or deposit the minimum capital of EUR 12,000. The bank must issue a certificate confirming the deposit and the block on withdrawal until the company is registered and the notary releases the funds. The certificate must be addressed to the Luxembourg notary.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Passport or national ID of each shareholder and director
Proof of residential address
AML/KYC declarations
Bank account opening forms and source of funds documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank AML queries by providing enhanced due diligence documentation; if proof of funds is insufficient, supplement with sworn declarations or audited statements and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) with authority to authenticate corporate deeds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Coordinate a notarial appointment. All subscribers and directors must appear before the notary to sign the deed of incorporation and the articles of association. The notary will verify legal capacity, capital deposit certificate, registered office availability, and the legality of the corporate purpose. The deed must be approved before filing with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Bank capital deposit certificate
Identity documents of all subscribing shareholders and managers
Draft articles of association and corporate purpose
Consent of the registered office provider or landlord
Auditors report (for in-kind contributions) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the deed, prepare and execute a supplementary notarial deed correcting the defect; no separate filing fee is imposed except statutory notary fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via the eJustice online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, submit the notarial deed and statutory forms to the RCS through the eJustice portal. The application must include the proposed legal form (SARL), registered office address, directors, capital structure, and corporate object (customs brokerage). The RCS assigns the company’s registration number after legal review.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles
Identification of directors and managers
Consent forms and specimen signatures of managers
Proof of registered office (lease or sublease)
Civil liability declarations if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, respond within 15 days via the eJustice portal with corrected documents; re-submission is processed on a best-effort basis. If the registration is refused, a formal appeal may be filed with the District Court of Luxembourg within 3 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the official gazette (Mémorial C – Recueil des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers acting as publication authority for the Mémorial C
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically forwards the registration extract for publication in the electronic Mémorial C. The publication contains the articles in abbreviated form, legal entity details, and registered office. This publication constitutes legal publicity and is a precondition for the company’s capacity to invoke its articles against third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarized articles of association
Confirmation from the RCS of publication queue
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette extract contains errors, submit a request for rectification via the RCS portal, supported by a notarial extract and the original registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, EORI and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Administration des douanes et accises for EORI; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) for employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, apply for a Luxembourg VAT number with the AEDT. Apply for an EORI number through the Customs and Excise Agency website or via IMS (Import Management System). Register as an employer with the CCSS within 8 days of hiring, and register for corporate income tax and municipal business tax (taxe d’abonnement) as applicable.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Articles of association and notarial deed
Identity of directors and authorized signatories
Business plan and customs brokerage activity description
Bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Coordinate with the tax import and distribution administration to clarify any EORI or VAT data mismatch; submit a formal amendment request and provide proof of business address and customs activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs brokerage license application and establishment permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des douanes et accises (Customs and Excise Agency) under the Ministry of Finance; Ministry of the Economy for the autorisation d’établissement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a prior authorization application for commercial establishment under Luxembourg law, then apply for a customs broker license. Submit the company’s incorporation documents, proof of professional competence of the responsible manager, a physical premises inspection, and a surety bond or financial guarantee, together with AML/compliance manuals and a customs procedure description.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Articles of association
Criminal record and solvency evidence for directors/managers
Professional qualifications or experience certificates in customs brokerage
Premises lease and floor plan
AML/KYC compliance policy manual
Surety bond or bank guarantee
Customs broker license application form and AEO certificate if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license application is queried, provide an explanatory memorandum and additional compliance evidence within 15 days; if refused, appeal to the Minister of Finance and subsequently to the administrative tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l’Économie) for the establishment permit; Administration des douanes et accises under the Ministry of Finance for the customs brokerage license
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d’établissement (business establishment permit) and Licence de commissionnaire en douane (customs brokerage license)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l’environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Classified establishment declaration (registered), for a customs brokerage house using office, bonded warehouse and non-industrial transit handling premises; a full EIA is only required if chemical or hazardous substances are handled on site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with municipal discharge thresholds and the general rules of the Luxembourg water management administration; volatile organic compounds (VOCs) must remain below 50 mg C/Nm³ at emission points; hazardous waste, including customs-seized or trans-loaded goods, must be handled in approved containers and disposed of by licensed waste operators. Firewater catchments and spill containment measures must be in place.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Corps grand-ducal d’incendie et de secours (CGDIS) verifying emergency exits, extinguishing systems, and evacuation plans; structural load inspection for any racking or bonded storage area; workplace safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) confirming safe access, handling equipment, personal protective equipment, and staff training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties, and excise; central business registration portal: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / MyGuichet.lu; customs authority: Administration des douanes et accises (Customs and Excise Administration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an SARL must first execute incorporation before a Luxembourg notary and file with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS). The RCS issues a registration number which triggers notification to the AEDT for VAT and registration duties. The ACD subsequently attributes a national direct-tax identification number (matricule). For non-resident entities with no fixed establishment, direct VAT registration with the AEDT is required, with appointment of a local VAT representative if even one taxable transaction is performed in Luxembourg. The EORI number must be obtained separately for customs activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. An SARL is a statutory capital company subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax at entity level. No pass-through election exists. Available elections include: (1) joint election for VAT group registration (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the VAT Code for closely linked entities; (2) election for fiscal unity under Article 164bis LIR for resident parent-subsidiary groups holding at least 75% shareholding; and (3) option for the 30,000 EUR small-undertaking VAT exemption (which is generally inadvisable for a B2B customs brokerage). Hybrid mismatch elections and CFC rules are governed by the ATAD implementation law of 21 December 2018 and do not provide elective reclassification of entity status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Code (Loi modifiée du 12 février 1979 concernant la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), implementing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No universal turnover registration threshold applies: a taxable person whose annual turnover (excluding VAT) does not exceed EUR 30,000 may benefit from the small undertaking exemption, but VAT registration remains mandatory without threshold for non-established taxable persons, for intra-Community acquisitions, for receipt of services subject to reverse charge, and for any taxable person who waives the exemption. A customs brokerage SARL will generally be mandatorily registered because its B2B services fall within the general reverse-charge regime and cross-border activities require a VAT identification number.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate. E-invoicing is permitted under EU rules and B2B e-invoicing is not yet mandatory. VAT returns must be filed electronically via the FEDeRation (Déclaration TVA) XML gateway; EC Sales Lists (recapitulatif) must be filed electronically through eCDF. Customs declarations are lodged via the EU Customs Decision System / Import Control System 2 / AES (Automated Export System); certified customs brokers must connect through the Customs Information System with an EORI number, use authorized electronic message formats, and comply with the electronic filing mandatory for customs operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating may be claimed for (a) supplies of goods dispatched or transported outside the EU by or on behalf of the supplier, provided the goods leave the EU customs territory; (b) intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-registered customer with a valid EU VAT ID and submission of the EC Sales List; (c) auxiliary transport and ancillary services directly related to exports and intra-Community supplies, including customs brokerage, forwarding, warehousing, and transit services performed directly for the exporter or consignee; and (d) services performed by customs brokers as intermediaries where the underlying supply qualifies for zero-rating and all statutory proof requirements are met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document – SAD/DAU) with MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical dispatch
Proof of departure from EU customs territory (customs office endorsement, exit summary declaration, T1 transit document)
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent banking evidence of receipt of payment from the foreign counterparty
Commercial invoice and VAT invoice complying with Articles 43-44 of the VAT Code
EORI number and, where applicable, customs brokerage power of attorney issued by the exporter
Proof of the counterparty's VAT registration for intra-Community supplies (valid VAT ID and EC Sales List)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may conduct an audit typically within a 6-year assessment window (extendable to 10 years in case of fraud or undeclared taxable transactions). Incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger repayment of under-declared VAT plus default interest at the statutory rate of 3.0% per annum. Administrative penalties range from EUR 750 up to the amount of evaded tax; in cases of deliberate fraud, penalties may reach 100% of the evaded VAT. Criminal liability attaches under Article 89 of the VAT Code, with imprisonment up to 5 years for tax fraud. Customs authorities may impose separate penalties for false export declarations, including forfeiture of goods and suspension or revocation of the customs broker license.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — the Luxembourg central bank and national member of the Eurosystem — exercising prudential and macro-prudential oversight of resident credit institutions jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), the competent Luxembourg authority for AML/CFT supervision, licensing and supervision of banks, payment institutions and electronic money institutions (EMIs), and enforcement of CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing. The BCL operates the TARGET2-Luxembourg settlement system, manages the euro-liquidity window for resident banks, and collects balance-of-payments and external-stats reporting from resident credit institutions under the BCL external statistics regulation (implementing the BPM6/Eurostat classification framework).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates a fully liberalised euro-area currency regime with complete convertibility on both current and capital account. No exchange-control authorisation, BCL permit, or CSSF approval is required for cross-border transfers, dividend distributions, royalty or interest payments, repayment of shareholder advances, or repatriation of equity on liquidation. Eurozone membership and Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union guarantee free movement of capital and payments; conversion is subject only to standard bank-side AML/KYC screening, EU-wide targeted financial sanctions, and statistical declaration thresholds. The only genuine profit-remittance tax hurdle is the domestic 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, which is reduced to 0% for qualifying EU/EEA parent companies under Directive 2011/96/EU (subject to a 12-month holding period, minimum participation and substance/anti-abuse conditions) and to 5% for eligible US corporate shareholders under the Luxembourg–US income tax treaty; direct dividend and service-fee payments are otherwise unlimited in amount and currency. A customs brokerage SARL may therefore invoice and receive in EUR, USD, CNY, GBP, CHF or any freely convertible currency without central-bank approval, provided each flow is properly documented to substantiate the underlying UCC customs activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export receivables may remain indefinitely in foreign currency in a properly declared resident account, may be converted into euro at the commercial interbank rate, or may be netted under genuine back-to-back offset structures. The BCL external statistics regime (pursuant to the BCL regulation on external statistics, applying BPM6/Eurostat codes) obliges the resident credit institution to classify each export or service-receipt flow and report it to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes; this is purely a statistical reporting obligation and not a conversion mandate. The practical compliance burden for the Luxembourg customs brokerage entity is documentary: recurring foreign-currency receipts should be matched to the corresponding commercial invoice, UCC customs declarations, DELTA/eCustoms records, CMR/airway bills, and the brokerage service contract so that the bank's monitoring system does not flag the flows as unexplained third-party payments or trade-based money laundering.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.additional_banking_compliance_context: The customs brokerage SARL is classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced under Luxembourg AML taxonomy. The onboarding bank will apply enhanced due diligence because the entity collects third-party client monies destined for customs duties, VAT, and excise settlement, a structure historically associated with trade-based money laundering. The entity must therefore present a binding client-money escrow agreement, a functional MLRO designation, verified UBO documentation, an ADA/EORI operating record, and a demonstrable Luxembourg substance package.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.bank_account_structure_recommendation: The treasury blueprint should establish three distinct banking silos: (i) an operational EUR/USD professional current account for own revenue and operating expenses; (ii) a segregated client-money escrow account (compte séquestre) holding duties, taxes, and transport-advance funds with contractual dual-signature governance; and (iii) a trade-settlement and customs-bond facility supporting documentary credit issuance, standby guarantees for the ADA, and FX hedging execution. This tri-silo structure reduces AML friction, facilitates clean audit trails, and satisfies CSSF-adjacent money-guarding expectations even though the broker itself is not a regulated financial institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.cross_border_treasury_policy_note: All treasury movements should be executed through tier-1 Luxembourg credit institutions or their EU branches, with prohibition of client funds passing through non-EEA payment processors or unregulated digital wallets. Currency conversion should be executed with transparent cost disclosure, and any active FX exposure must result only from the natural mismatch between duty liabilities, client funds, and brokerage fees; speculative open positions are inadmissible for a licensed customs-service SME.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.liquidity_clearing_rules: The SARL is subject to the UCC requirement of being established in the customs territory of the Union, and all duty settlements must be traceable to the taxpayer importer of record. The recommended clearing configuration uses SWIFT gpi with UETR for international wires, SEPA CT/SEPA Inst for euro-area operational flows, TARGET2 for high-value inbound capital injections, and a dedicated ADA deferment account (compte de reports) for regular periodic payment of duties and excises rather than per-declaration wires.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.fx_hedging_governance: Any FX hedging must be justified by an underlying commercial exposure, approved by the SARL's management resolution, and documented in a simple internal hedging policy. The SARL will likely qualify as an NFC under EMIR; the bank or broker dealer will classify it either as a retail, professional, or elective professional client under MiFID II, and the hedging documentation set will include ISDA with CSA where uncleared derivative margin rules apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.contingency_banking_and_regulatory_notes: Should the primary tier-1 bank decline the file due to enhanced-risk appetite constraints, the backup path is a mid-tier Luxembourg bank or a private-banking institution, paired with a specialised trade-finance house. Regulatory fallback includes approaching the CSSF for guidance on e-money institution safeguarding limitations, and the BCL for statistical-code clarification on complex equity injections. Neither the CSSF nor the BCL provides passporting or licensing relief for unregulated offshore EMIs, which cannot be used as a primary treasury rail for duty settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.stage_exit_criteria: Stage 4 is complete when the SARL has executed a mandate with at least one tier-1 Luxembourg bank, opened the tri-silo account structure, obtained a dedicated escrow agreement approved by compliance, completed the in-person KYC interview, secured the ADA-specific customs bond or standby LC, documented the inbound capital injection purpose codes, and concluded an FX line with a licensed counterparty including the ISDA/CSA documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.final_treasury_business_rule: Inbound capital injections flow exclusively from the identified UBO/shareholder's own account with matching board resolutions; outbound duty payments flow exclusively from the escrow account with per-transaction customs-declaration references; brokerage fee revenue is swept daily to the operational account; and any FX conversion is executed through the bank or a G-SIB counterparty within pre-approved limits. This rule set should be encoded into the future operating procedures and submitted to the bank's annual compliance review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes and management report) approved by shareholders and filed in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); simplified format permitted for small companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve the annual accounts within 6 months after the balance-sheet date (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); RCS filing must occur within 1 month after approval (by 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing is prosecuted by the Luxembourg Public Prosecutor's Office; court-ordered filing and criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 may be imposed, and sustained non-compliance can lead to administrative strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual combined direct tax return covering corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year SARL: mandatory electronic filing due by 31 December of the year following the taxable year; reasoned extension requests may be granted by the tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax, late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (or pro-rata), administrative fines, and official assessment by the ACD where the return is omitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (annual declaration number 2022) for periodic VAT taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) – Luxembourg VAT Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayers: annual VAT return due by 30 April of the following year; monthly or quarterly periodic VAT returns remain due for each relevant settlement period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, administrative fines per late or missing declaration, suspension of VAT refunds, and criminal proceedings for repeated non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO register declaration and updates (declaration of beneficial owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 30 days of incorporation; update within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; Luxembourg law imposes no separate annual re-filing requirement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines and imprisonment for knowing omission or false UBO data, publication of non-compliance on the LBR portal, and practical blocking of RCS filings while the register is inaccurate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting approving the annual accounts, with signed minutes entered in the corporate minute book (internal statutory deliverable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records maintained at the registered office; no separate RCS filing of ordinary AGM minutes unless the resolutions require registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within 6 months of the balance-sheet date (calendar-year SARL: by 30 June); minutes must be signed and permanently retained in the minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM on time is an offence under the amended Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, punishable by court fines; persistent default may ground judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs brokerage license status and customs guarantee/security maintenance applicable to the licensed customs brokerage house
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration) with oversight under the Union Customs Code
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual licence filing; customs broker authorization and any customs debt security must remain continuously valid; annual internal verification is recommended at year-end before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or revocation of the customs brokerage authorization, forfeiture of customs guarantees, loss of authorized economic operator advantages, and refusal of customs clearance privileges for non-availability of a valid security

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé applies when the SARL exceeds at least two of the three size criteria on the balance-sheet date for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory for public-interest entities, for companies whose articles of association so require, and where sector-specific AML/CFT licensing obligations demand it
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the amended law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts (transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS is mandatory for listed consolidated groups and permitted for individual annual accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg imposes event-driven RBE filing (update within 30 days of any UBO change) rather than an annual statutory re-filing. Annual protocol: before the AGM, the managers re-certify the UBO table, reconcile it with the Register of Members and any share transfers (including usufruct and indirect holding chains) completed during the year, and file an RBE update if a change occurred; a no-change confirmation is documented in the signed AGM minutes
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des associés) – compulsory for SARL share ownership records
Register of Directors/Managers and current RCS extract – maintained on site to evidence authorised signatories
Minute Book (procès-verbaux of general meetings and management decisions) – signed originals permanently retained

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 6,000 (typical annual range for a Luxembourg registered-office or domiciliation service provider, excluding bank, notary and accounting fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 16,000 (typical certified audit fee for a small-to-mid-size Luxembourg SARL; not applicable where the statutory size exemptions are met and no sector-specific audit duty applies)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined: 17% corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), 7% solidarity surcharge on the corporate income tax (effective 1.1875%), and 6.75% municipal business tax (Luxembourg City base rate).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption under Sec. 166 LIR: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains on shares held at least 12 months in companies subject to comparable tax and with at least 10% participation or acquisition cost above €6 million. Additional incentives include a 25% innovation investment credit and a 10% tax credit for net wealth tax on qualifying financial assets.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward; deductible against future profits with compulsory denunciation if the loss-making business activity is changed)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 660 (Municipal Business Tax Return), electronically filed via the MyGuichet.lu portal or the statutory ACD professional e-filing channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months of the fiscal year-end (31 May for calendar-year taxpayers); extensions up to 31 December of the following year are available on formal application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, registered office, Luxembourg RCS number, tax matriculation number, legal form (SARL).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg PE of a foreign company, enter the PE address and foreign registration number in the dedicated annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss before taxation as per the Luxembourg statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the separate PE financial statements; translate foreign currency at the official ECB annual average rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends and capital gains qualifying for the 100% participation exemption, including associated foreign withholding tax (covered by treaty or EU directive).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a statement of the participation, holding period, and the effective taxation of the subsidiary in its residence country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable basis after adding back non-deductible expenses (taxes, fines, excessive directors' fees) and deducting available loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply a pro-rated loss compensation if the Luxembourg PE has a different fiscal history from the head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessment base for municipal business tax, usually equal to the taxable income plus 2% of interest on long-term debt and certain royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute separately for each Luxembourg municipality where the PE operates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine €250–€2,500 (up to €5,000 in case of recurrence); late payment: 9% annual interest on the unpaid amount, plus 3/6/9/12% staggered surcharge after; fraud: 50% penalty on evaded tax on top of 9% interest and possible criminal fine of up to €250,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends distributed by a Luxembourg SARL to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (≥10% ownership, 12-month holding period) or to 5% under DTA provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Claim by submitting Form 901 (demande de remboursement / exonération) to the Luxembourg tax authorities before distribution, accompanied by a certificate of residence (TRC) from the shareholder's tax authority, evidence of shareholding, and holding-period proof; the paying agent (transfer agent or bank) must retain the exemption certificate; US shareholders may use Form W-8BEN-E/8833.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding on interest (including loans, bonds, cash deposits) and royalties paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-residents, provided the payments are at arm's length; profit-participating instruments or constructive dividends may still be reclassified as dividends (15% WHT).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File when the Luxembourg-resident member is part of an MNE group whose consolidated turnover exceeds €750 million; preparation required upon demand if the local entity has revenue below €1.5 million and exceptional characteristics.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not enact a separate Economic Substance Regulations law, but tax residence, OECD BEPS, and EU anti-abuse doctrines apply (Art. 6 Abgabenordnung, EU directive ATAD, and CJEU jurisprudence). A customs brokerage SARL must demonstrate adequate premises, qualified staff, operational independence, and risk management commensurate with its receipts; a pure shell exercising no real control over customs brokerage contracts will be disregarded, and its payments may be recast as constructive dividends.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting commission income, fabricating expenses, preparing false Box 16 declarations, or destroying records to avoid corporate tax and customs VAT on brokerage services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment up to 10 years back; evasion penalty equal to 50% of the evaded tax (25% if spontaneous disclosure), 20% penalty for incomplete declarations, 9% annual interest; criminal fine up to €250,000, imprisonment up to 5 years (Art. 187 of the General Tax Law / Art. 405 of the Criminal Code).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certified false financial statements are jointly and severally liable for the corporate liability, are subject to travel bans, prohibition of leaving Luxembourg while under investigation, and may be sentenced to 5 years’ imprisonment; the corporate veil may be disregarded under Art. 18 of the Tax Adaptation Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SARL with nominal work force and no real business purpose exclusively to channel royalties, dividends, or customs fees from EEA parent/subsidiaries to a zero-tax jurisdiction without any non-tax business justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax residence, DTA benefits and EU directive exemptions; reclassification of all flows as constructive dividends subject to 15% WHT; 100% surcharge on the under-declared tax and 9% interest; potential notification to the anti-abuse network of the DAC-6 regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally assessed for the resulting tax if the entity is deemed a test tube (société écran); personal assets may be seised and managers may face imprisonment up to 3 years for abusing signals of law (abus de droit) under Art. 8 of the General Tax Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany customs brokerage commissions at non-arm's length, allocating excessive management fees to a Luxembourg parent, misappropriating the group's profit ratio by artificially inflating customs value, or materially failing to produce Local File despite the threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment by the tax administration; secondary adjustment reclassifying the excess as a loan or dividend (15% WHT); fine of 25% of the adjustment, increasing to 50% for bad faith; country-to-country reporting penalty of up to €25,000 per unjustified failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve off-market pricing may be liable under general tort (Art. 1382 of the Civil Code); in the event of insolvency, liquidators or tax office may call on the directors' personal liability for the unpaid corporate tax plus penalties, and if fraud is proven, 5 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CTF Non-Compliance & Licence Violation in Customs Brokerage
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct CDD/EDD on customers in a customs brokerage business; processing payments for sanctioned goods or disguised cash; operating without the statutory customs broker licence; manipulating customs valuation to reduce duties and VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imposition of large VAT and customs penalties (up to twice the evaded duties), revocation of the customs licence, AML administrative fines up to €5 million or 10% of turnover (Law of 12 November 2004 as amended); criminal confiscation of goods and up to 5 years' imprisonment for money laundering, extended to 10 years for organised crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal criminal conviction, disqualification from commercial activity, travel restriction, and confiscation of personal assets; Luxembourg courts allow the lifting of the corporate veil in case of abuse of the company's personality to commit illegality, resulting in joint liability.
